etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English byen, from Old English bycġan (“to buy, pay for, acquire, redeem, ransom, procure, get done, sell”), from Proto-West Germanic *buggjan, from Proto-Germanic *bugjaną (“to buy”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *bʰūgʰ- (“to bend”), or from Proto-Indo-European *bʰewgʰ- (“to take away, deliver”).

Cognate with Scots buy (“to buy, purchase”), obsolete Dutch beugen (“to buy”), Old Saxon buggian, buggean (“to buy”), Old Norse byggja (“to build, settle”), Gothic 𐌱𐌿𐌲𐌾𐌰𐌽 (bugjan, “to buy”). The spelling with “u” is from the Southwest, while the pronunciation with /aɪ/ is from the East Midlands.

definitions.definition: (transitive, ditransitive) To obtain (something) in exchange for money or goods.

quote.text: Buy what thou hast no need of, and ere long thou wilt sell thy necessaries.

definitions.definition: (transitive, ditransitive) To obtain, especially by some sacrifice.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Proverbs 23:23:
quote.text: Buy the truth and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.

definitions.definition: (transitive, archaic) To suffer consequences for (something) through being deprived of something; to pay for (something one has done).

quote.citation: 1593, anonymous author, The Life and Death of Iacke Straw […], Act I:
quote.text: VVhat villaine, doſt ſtrike me? I ſweare by the rood,As I am Iacke Strawe, thou ſhalt buy it with thy blood.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To be equivalent to in value.
(transitive, informal) to accept as true; to believe

quote.citation: 2020, Akwaeke Emezi, The Death of Vivek Oji, Faber & Faber Ltd, page 201:
quote.text: People like to say that dead people look asleep, and maybe she would have bought that under different circumstances.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To make a purchase or purchases, to treat (for a drink, meal or gift)
(poker slang, transitive) To make a bluff, usually a large one.
Something which is bought; a purchase.
